sentences.text:
The Prin. Secy. Home, Lucknow
Counsel for Applicant :- Aman Kumar Shrivastav,Suraj Singh Visen
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
It is alleged in the FIR that daughter of the informant was married on 08.06.2019 with the son of the applicant Mukesh Kumar.
The deceased was subjected to cruelty relating to demand of dowry on 07.04.2023.
While the informant was trying to call his daughter for knowing her well being, he was informed that she has committed suicide.
Cause of death is strangulation.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is mother-in-law of the deceased aged about 70 years.
She has been falsely implicated.

The complainant PW-1 (father of the deceased)
PW-2 and PW-3 (brothers of the deceased) have not supported the prosecution case at all.
They Sheela Kannaujia vs State Of U.P. Thru.

Their statements are on record as Annexure No. RA-1 to RA-3 to the rejoinder affidavit.

It is further submitted that the applicant is languishing in jail since 05.07.2023 without having any criminal history; there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released from jail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, she shall not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned AGA has opposed the bail application submitting that cause of death is strangulation and there are antemortem injuries and the deceased died within seven years of marriage due to demand of dowry, however, he does not dispute the fact that fact witnesses PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 have not supported the prosecution case at all during their cross examination before the Court.

On due consideration to the statement of the PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 as well as considering the fact that the applicant is languishing in jail since 05.07.2023 without having any criminal antecedent and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant, Sheela Kannaujia, involved in Case Crime/FIR No. 225/2023, under Sections 498A/304-B/302 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station - Umari Begumganj, District - Gonda,
be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through her counsel.

In case of her absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.
Sheela Kannaujia vs State Of U.P. Thru.
